title: Making Cordmarked Pottery
scope: Original exhibit text, including forming, drying and credits. Developer is potter who made shown replicas; not a generic blog or merely archaeological inference.
supports: Replication coils with paddle/anvil. Base and intermediate coils partly dry before more height; cold/wet conditions may stretch forming to two days. Finished greenware dries several days to a week. Reported worked example took about nine days from start through firing.

conditions.forming: coils, paddle and anvil, sometimes scraping

doesNotVerify: No specimen-matched weather, wet density, work-time log or failure denominator. Reported 2–4 mm archaeological walls use skilled paddle/anvil techniques, not evidence that unsupported beginner coils stand at that thickness.

evidence.shortExcerpt: The completed "greenware" pot is allowed to dry for several days or a week before it can be fired.
evidence.locator: Forming the pot; Credits and Sources; page dated 21 January 2003
